top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a mechanism that can be stated in physical terms: a small molecule forms a ternary complex between a target and an E3 ligase, ubiquitin is transferred and the proteasome disposes of the target. It has two decades of independent confirmation, and cereblon explains the glue strand, so one citation on induced proximity covers both. Crews, Deshaies and Handa is the most defensible three-name cut, though the lack of an approved PROTAC and the exclusion of Ciulli remain real weaknesses. Base editing is second for its clear single reaction, lipid nanoparticles third for maturity but with entangled attribution, and no award is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; only a Stockholm University colleague link to Xiaodong Zou, whose preferred zeolite proposal P003 I rank fifth
